title: Water Damage Mitigation Antimicrobial Line: Billed Area and Line Amount
content:
**Water Damage Mitigation — the tear-out antimicrobial line**

1. Antimicrobial is billed only on tiers where antimicrobial treatment is required.
2. The surfaces a tear-out exposes are treated once and billed as one tear-out antimicrobial line in square feet, dated the service date of the job's latest flood cut line, or of its latest pad removal line when it has no flood cut line, or of its latest carpet removal line when it has neither; a job that already carries an antimicrobial line, or that carries no pad removal, carpet removal or flood cut line, is billed no tear-out antimicrobial line.
3. The treated floor is the affected floor area mapped on the job. The treated wall and ceiling area is zero. The coverage factor is 1. The unit rate is the tier's antimicrobial rate per square foot.
4. The billed square feet are the treated floor plus the treated wall and ceiling area, multiplied by the coverage factor and rounded to two decimals, half up; the unit rate is multiplied by every rate multiplier that applies to the line and rounded to the cent, half up; the line amount is the billed square feet multiplied by that rounded unit rate, rounded to the cent, half up.
5. Amounts are rounded to the cent, half up.

## When no line is billed
| Situation | Tear-out antimicrobial line |
|---|---|
| The tier does not require antimicrobial treatment | none |
| The job already carries an antimicrobial line | none |
| The job carries no pad removal, carpet removal or flood cut line | none |

## Worked figure (hypothetical job)
Inputs chosen for illustration: an affected floor area of 733 square feet, an assumed antimicrobial rate of $0.47 per square foot and no rate multiplier applying.
- Billed square feet: 733 plus zero, multiplied by 1, that is 733.00.
- Unit rate: $0.47.
- Line amount: 733.00 multiplied by $0.47 is 344.51, so $344.51.

The billed square feet are fixed to two decimals and the unit rate to the cent before the two are multiplied, and the product is then rounded to the cent.
